questions.question: What does lazy loading mean in JPA?
options: Related data is read only when the code first uses it
Related data is never read from the database
Related data is read together with the parent in the same query
Related data is cached forever after the first request
questions.explanation: Lazy loading delays the query for related data until you touch the association.

questions.question: Which pair shows the default fetch types of @OneToMany and @ManyToOne?
questions.explanation: Collections are lazy by default and single-valued links such as @ManyToOne are eager by default.

questions.question: A Restaurant has a lazy dishes collection and an eager chefs collection. Inside one transaction the code calls findById, then chefs.size(), then dishes.size(). How many SQL statements run in total?
questions.explanation: The restaurant and its eager chefs come in one query, and touching the lazy dishes runs one more, so the total is 2.

questions.question: A service method has no @Transactional. It loads a Restaurant with findById and then prints restaurant.getDishes().size(), where dishes is lazy. What happens?
options: It prints 0 because the collection is empty
It works, because Spring keeps the session open forever
It throws a LazyInitializationException because the session is closed
It throws a NullPointerException because dishes is null
questions.explanation: The entity is detached after the repository call ends, so the lazy collection cannot run its query.

questions.question: To stop a LazyInitializationException, a teammate changes every association in the project to FetchType.EAGER. What is the main risk?
options: Every query loads more rows, and it can cause the N+1 problem
Lazy loading becomes impossible to turn on again
questions.explanation: Eager everywhere hides the error but makes every query heavier, so fetch extra data per query with JOIN FETCH or an entity graph.
